title: So and not as substitutes for clauses
summary: so и not как заменители придаточных: I think so / I hope not / I'm afraid so, if so / if not, ограничения (know, doubt) и стилистика.
ru:
## so вместо целого придаточного
После глаголов мнения и предположения слово **so** заменяет придаточное с *that*. Так мы отвечаем коротко и не повторяем сказанное.
> A: Will it rain tomorrow? B: I think **so**. (= I think it will rain tomorrow.) — Думаю, да.
> A: Has she lost her job? B: I'm afraid **so**. — Боюсь, что да.
Так ведут себя **think, believe, expect, suppose, imagine, guess** (американский вариант), **hope, be afraid, seem, appear**: *I believe so, I expect so, I suppose so, I hope so, It appears so.*

## Отрицательный ответ: два способа
Для отрицания есть две схемы, и выбирать нужно по глаголу.
| Глагол | Отрицание | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| think, believe, expect, suppose, imagine, guess | **don't + V + so** (обычно) или **V + not** (формально) | I don't think so. / I think not. |
| hope, be afraid | только **V + not** | I hope not. / I'm afraid not. |
Ошибка русскоговорящих — калька «не надеюсь»: ~~I don't hope so.~~ → **I hope not.** Выражение *I'm afraid not* — вежливое «нет, к сожалению»; *I'm afraid so* — «да, к сожалению» (плохие новости). *I hope so* — «да, и я этого хочу», *I hope not* — «нет, и слава богу».
> A: Is the strike going to affect flights? B: I hope **not**. — Надеюсь, что нет.
> A: Do you think they'll agree? B: I **don't expect so**. / I **expect not**.

## say, tell и другие глаголы речи
**so** встречается и после глаголов речи, часто в устойчивых формулах: *I told you so! · If you say so. · He said so himself. · So they say. · So I've heard. · Why do you say so?* Но *so* не заменяет придаточное после **know, be sure, doubt, deny**: ~~I know so.~~ → *I know.* ~~I doubt so.~~ → *I doubt it.* ~~I'm sure so.~~ → *I'm sure of it.*

## if so и if not
**If so** = «если это так, если да», **if not** = «если нет». Это компактный способ не повторять условие.
> Are you over 18? **If so**, you can register online. **If not**, ask a parent to do it.
> Do you have a visa? If not, you must apply now.
Так же работают *perhaps so / perhaps not, probably so / probably not, certainly not, of course not, absolutely not*: *A: Will they come? B: Perhaps so.*

## Нюансы стиля
- *I think so* — нейтральный, чуть неуверенный ответ; *I think not* звучит формально и немного книжно, в разговоре его почти заменяет *I don't think so*.
- *I guess so* типично для американского английского. *I suppose so* часто выражает неохотное согласие.
- *So* может стоять в начале: *So I understand. So I believe. So it seems.* — «насколько я понимаю».
- Не оставляйте ответ голым: ~~I think.~~ → *I think so.*; ~~I hope.~~ → *I hope so.* ~~I think it~~ тоже неверно.
en:
## so instead of a whole clause
After verbs of opinion and expectation **so** replaces a *that*-clause. It lets us answer briefly without repeating.
> A: Will it rain tomorrow? B: I think **so**. (= I think it will rain tomorrow.)
> A: Has she lost her job? B: I'm afraid **so**.
This works with **think, believe, expect, suppose, imagine, guess** (especially AmE), **hope, be afraid, seem, appear**: *I believe so, I expect so, I suppose so, I hope so, It appears so.*

## Negative answers: two patterns
| Verb | Negative | Example |
|---|---|---|
| think, believe, expect, suppose, imagine, guess | **don't + verb + so** (usual) or **verb + not** (formal) | I don't think so. / I think not. |
| hope, be afraid | only **verb + not** | I hope not. / I'm afraid not. |
Learners often translate Russian "не надеюсь": ~~I don't hope so.~~ → **I hope not.** *I'm afraid not* is a polite "no, unfortunately"; *I'm afraid so* is "yes, unfortunately" (bad news). *I hope so* = "yes, and I want it"; *I hope not* = "no, and I'm glad".
> A: Is the strike going to affect flights? B: I hope **not**.
> A: Do you think they'll agree? B: I **don't expect so**. / I **expect not**.

## say, tell and other speech verbs
**so** also appears after verbs of saying, often in fixed phrases: *I told you so! · If you say so. · He said so himself. · So they say. · So I've heard. · Why do you say so?* But *so* does not replace the clause after **know, be sure, doubt, deny**: ~~I know so.~~ → *I know.* ~~I doubt so.~~ → *I doubt it.* ~~I'm sure so.~~ → *I'm sure of it.*

## if so and if not
**If so** = "if that is the case", **if not** = "if it is not". They save us repeating the condition.
> Are you over 18? **If so**, you can register online. **If not**, ask a parent to do it.
> Do you have a visa? If not, you must apply now.
The same holds for *perhaps so / perhaps not, probably so / probably not, certainly not, of course not, absolutely not*.

## Style notes
- *I think so* is neutral and a little tentative; *I think not* sounds formal and bookish, and in speech *I don't think so* is normal.
- *I guess so* is typical of American English. *I suppose so* often shows reluctant agreement.
- *So* can also open a sentence: *So I understand. So I believe. So it seems.*
- Do not leave the answer bare: ~~I think.~~ → *I think so.*; ~~I hope.~~ → *I hope so.*
structure:
## Положительный и отрицательный ответ
| Глагол | Да | Нет |
|---|---|---|
| think | I think so. | I don't think so. / I think not. |
| believe / expect / suppose / imagine | I believe so. | I don't believe so. / I believe not. |
| guess (AmE) | I guess so. | I guess not. |
| hope | I hope so. | I hope not. |
| be afraid | I'm afraid so. | I'm afraid not. |
| seem / appear | It seems so. | It seems not. |

## Другие формулы
| Форма | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| If so / If not | «если да / если нет» | If not, call me. |
| Perhaps / Probably + so / not | «возможно, да / нет» | Perhaps not. |
| told / said + you so | «я же говорил» | I told you so. |
| doubt + it | «сомневаюсь» | I doubt it. |

## Формулы
> **think / believe / expect / suppose + so**  ·  **don't + think / believe / expect / suppose + so**
> **hope / be afraid + so**  ·  **hope / be afraid + not**

exercises.title: so или not?

items.text: A: Is the shop open on Sunday? B: I think {{so}}.
A: Will they win the final? B: I hope {{not}}. I've bet on the other team.
A: Has the flight been cancelled? B: I'm afraid {{so}}.
A: Do you think he'll resign? B: I don't think {{so}}.
A: Is it going to snow tonight? B: I hope {{so}}. I love snow.
A: Did the meeting go well? B: I'm afraid {{not}}. It was a disaster.
A: Is she coming to the party? B: I suppose {{so}}, but she hasn't confirmed.
A: Will prices fall this year? B: I don't expect {{so}}.

exercises.example: A: Will she come? B: I hope ... (да, надеюсь) → I hope **so**.

exercises.title: if so, perhaps so и другое

items.text: Are you over eighteen? {{If so}}, you can register online.
Do you have a ticket? {{If not}}, you can buy one at the desk.
A: Will the trains be running? B: {{Perhaps|Maybe}} so; nobody knows yet.
I warned you it would fail; I {{told}} you so.
A: Money can't buy happiness. B: So they {{say}}.
A: Will you apply for the job? B: I'm {{afraid}} not; I don't have the qualifications.
A: Will she forgive him? B: I {{suppose}} not; she was very hurt.

items.q: A: Will it be cold tomorrow? B: I don't think ___.
items.why: После *think* отрицание строим как **don't think so**.

items.q: A: Is she angry? B: I hope ___. I don't want any more trouble.
items.why: Нам не нужен конфликт — значит, «надеюсь, что нет»: **I hope not**.

items.q: A: Are we late? B: I'm afraid ___. The film started ten minutes ago.
Какой ответ НЕверен? A: Is the museum free today? B: ...
items.why: С *hope* отрицание только **I hope not**: *I don't hope so* — ошибка.

items.q: A: Will he be promoted? B: I ___.
items.why: **I believe so** — глагол мнения в Present Simple и *so*.

items.q: I didn't invent this idea; the director said ___ himself.
items.why: **said so himself** — *so* заменяет придаточное «что это так»; *that* без придаточного фраза неполна.

items.q: A: Will you be at the conference? B: I'm afraid ___; I'll be abroad that week.
items.why: Не сможет прийти — «к сожалению, нет»: **I'm afraid not**.

items.q: A: Is the film suitable for kids? B: I ___.
A: Does he know the answer? B: I ___.
items.why: После *know* слово *so* не используется; здесь подходит **think so**.

items.q: Do you have a licence? ___, you can't rent a car.
A: Will the new law pass? B: I doubt ___.
A: Will the price go down? B: I expect ___; it has risen every year.
items.why: По контексту ответ отрицательный: **I expect not** (= *I don't expect so*).

exercises.title: Ответьте коротко
exercises.instruction: Дайте короткий ответ с **so** или **not**, подходящий по смыслу в скобках.

items.prompt: Will the bank be open on Saturday? (Я думаю, что да.)
Is the exam difficult? (К сожалению, да.)
Has Sam failed again? (Надеюсь, что нет.)
Will they cancel the festival? (Не думаю.)
Is she going to apologise? (Не ожидаю.)
Перепишите второе предложение с if so: Are you a student? If you are a student, you get a discount.
answers: If so, you get a discount.

exercises.title: Переведите на английский
exercises.instruction: Переведите на английский. Ключевые слова даны.

items.prompt: Ответьте на вопрос «Will it rain?»: Боюсь, что да.
Ответьте на вопрос «Is it serious?»: Надеюсь, что нет.
Ответьте на вопрос «Will she help us?»: Не думаю.

answers: If not, give me a call.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте на вопросы и покажите свою точку зрения, используя so / not. Образцы — для самопроверки.

items.prompt: Do you think your country will win the next big football tournament?
items.sample: I don't think so, but I hope so!

items.prompt: Is it going to rain at the weekend? Answer as if you checked the forecast.
items.sample: I'm afraid so. The forecast says it will rain all day.

items.prompt: Do you think technology will replace most teachers?
items.sample: I hope not. Teachers do much more than give information.

items.prompt: Do you have any plans for tomorrow? If so, say what. If not, say what you'd like to do.
items.sample: I don't, but if not, I'd like to visit a museum.

items.prompt: Write a short dialogue of two lines using I suppose so.
items.sample: A: Shall we go out for dinner? B: I suppose so, if you're not too tired.
